questions.question: Which mask should be entered for a /22 assignment?
questions.explanation: Six leading bits in the third octet total 252.

option_explanations.A: 248 contributes five one bits in the third octet, giving /21.
option_explanations.B: This mask contributes eight bits in each of the first three octets, giving /24.
option_explanations.C: Six leading bits in the third octet total 252.
option_explanations.D: 254 contributes seven one bits in the third octet, giving /23.

questions.question: How many IPv4 host bits does a /19 leave?

option_explanations.C: 11 host bits would leave a /21 prefix.
option_explanations.D: 21 host bits would leave a /11 prefix.

questions.question: Which prefix length should replace 255.255.255.248 in a diagram?
questions.explanation: The final octet 248 has five leading ones, giving 24 + 5 bits.

option_explanations.B: The final octet 248 has five leading ones, giving 24 + 5 bits.

questions.question: Which value is a valid contiguous IPv4 subnet mask?
questions.explanation: A valid prefix mask has an unbroken run of ones followed by zeros.

option_explanations.A: The third octet contains ones after the second octet has introduced zeros.
option_explanations.B: The fourth octet sets a one after the all-zero third octet.
option_explanations.C: 232 is 11101000 and has a one after a zero.
option_explanations.D: A valid prefix mask has an unbroken run of ones followed by zeros.

questions.question: A host at 192.0.2.142/27 sends to 192.0.2.157 with no overriding route. Which delivery decision is correct?

options.C: Treat the target as its own address
options.D: Treat the target as the subnet broadcast

questions.explanation: Both endpoints lie within the host range .129–.158 of 192.0.2.128/27.

option_explanations.A: A default route is unnecessary because both addresses are in .128–.159.
option_explanations.B: Both endpoints lie within the host range .129–.158 of 192.0.2.128/27.
option_explanations.C: The local address is .142, distinct from .157.

questions.question: A host at 198.51.100.94/27 uses gateway 198.51.100.65. Where does it send a frame for IPv4 destination 198.51.100.101?

options.C: To the Ethernet broadcast address for the entire IP packet
options.D: To the destination host's MAC learned by direct ARP

questions.explanation: The host is in the .64/27 network. Destination .101 is outside its connected range, so the next hop is the gateway.

option_explanations.A: The local MAC is the Ethernet source, not the next hop.
option_explanations.B: The host is in the .64/27 network. Destination .101 is outside its connected range, so the next hop is the gateway.
option_explanations.C: The host may broadcast an ARP request, but sends the routed IP packet in a unicast frame to its gateway.
option_explanations.D: Direct ARP would apply to an on-link destination, while .101 is outside .64–.95.

questions.question: Which octet contains both network and host bits in 172.20.89.7/20?
questions.explanation: Sixteen network bits cover the first two octets and four further bits are in octet three.

option_explanations.A: All eight bits of the fourth octet are host bits.
option_explanations.B: Sixteen network bits cover the first two octets and four further bits are in octet three.
option_explanations.C: All eight bits of the first octet belong to the prefix.
option_explanations.D: All eight bits of the second octet belong to the prefix.

questions.question: A is 198.51.100.61/26 and B is 198.51.100.70/25 on the same Ethernet. How do they classify each other's destination before ARP?

options.A: Both treat each other as remote
options.B: Both treat each other as local
options.C: A treats B as local and B treats A as remote
options.D: A treats B as remote and B treats A as local

questions.explanation: A's /26 ends at .63, while B's /25 includes both addresses.

option_explanations.C: It reverses the behavior of the /26 host and the /25 host.
option_explanations.D: A's /26 ends at .63, while B's /25 includes both addresses.

questions.question: Which is the longest prefix that puts 203.0.113.33 and 203.0.113.62 on the same subnet as usable hosts?
questions.explanation: Both addresses are usable in .32/27. A /28 divides them into separate blocks.

option_explanations.A: Both addresses are usable in .32/27. A /28 divides them into separate blocks.
option_explanations.C: /25 covers both addresses as usable hosts but includes more addresses than necessary.
option_explanations.D: /26 also covers both, but /27 is more specific.

questions.question: Which address is on-link for 172.19.47.32/21, assuming ordinary connected routing?
questions.explanation: A /21 advances by eight in octet three. The local block spans third octets 40 through 47.

option_explanations.A: A /21 advances by eight in octet three. The local block spans third octets 40 through 47.
option_explanations.B: The second octet differs from the fixed value 19.
option_explanations.D: 39 falls below the /21 block starting at third octet 40.
